scope: Follow-up to the earlier dormant privacy policy: consent-filtered native cache, account controls, targeted WebSocket lifecycle and contextual client presentation are now connected in source. This supersedes earlier statements that the publisher is not wired, not their historical test results.
implementation: Native cached projection exposes only enabled and game id/name, never paths or process inventory. Background detection, per-game permission and account permission must all allow publication; reads do not initiate scans. Expired, disabled or failed caches clear safely.

Authenticated per-connection sources use ordered lifecycle updates, leases, explicit selection timestamps and disconnect fallback. Targeted recipient policy checks blocking, visibility, friendship and server membership/overrides; server opt-out also applies to friends in server context. Old memberships default to no grant; new membership audience is persisted separately from future defaults.

Ready advertises the server epoch; updates require that epoch and increasing contextual revisions. Null tombstones, account-generation fences and legacy-server capability guards prevent stale grants and unsupported publication. User-supplied activity is not verified game ownership or execution.

Account-bound settings support actual membership search/sort, individual and bulk policies. Settings navigation collects short headings rather than field descriptions; controls use accessible names and responsive switches. Friend, member and profile surfaces consume only the exact authorized context.

Every invite join participates in the server lock protocol when supported; small-audience decisions use its transaction-bound count. Lock errors abort the join rather than bypass serialization; missing optional support leaves small denied. The own-membership sidebar projection exposes the persisted snapshot, and settings use explicit overrides first, then that snapshot; an enabled snapshot is no longer displayed as an unchecked control.
